ch12_lab_cmsbasics.title: Quick Check: CMS Architecture & Platform Choice

questions.q: What core architectural feature is what actually makes a piece of software a true CMS?
options: It has a colorful visual design
It separates content creation (stored in a database) from the code structure and design (stored in a Theme)
It runs entirely in the browser with no server
It only works for blogs, nothing else

questions.q: In the 3 tiers of web creation, which model is the 'Rental' model where the hosting company (like WordPress.com) manages everything for you?
options: No-Code Builder (Wix)
SaaS CMS (WordPress.com)
Self-Hosted CMS (WordPress.org)
Static HTML hosting

questions.q: If you switch a WordPress site to a completely different Theme, what happens to your existing blog posts and content?
options: All the content is permanently deleted
The content stays perfectly intact -- only the visual design changes, since content and design are stored separately
The content becomes uneditable
You have to re-upload the Media Library

questions.q: You want to announce a weekend coffee sale that expires on Sunday. Should you create a Post or a Page?
options: A Page, because sales are permanent information
A Post, because it's timely content meant for a reverse-chronological feed, not permanent like a Page
Neither -- sales go in the Theme settings
A Category

questions.q: Which organizational label is REQUIRED on every WordPress Post -- a Category or a Tag?
options: Category is required; Tags are optional
Tags are required; Categories are optional
Both are required
Neither is required

questions.q: What is the purpose of the WordPress 'Permalink' setting?
options: It permanently deletes old posts
It controls the structure of the URL (e.g., /about-us instead of /?p=123) for better SEO and readability
It locks the site so only Administrators can edit it
It sets the site's color scheme

ch12_lab_pluginsecurity.title: Quick Check: Child Themes, Plugins & Security

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a Child Theme in WordPress?
options: To make the site load faster
To preserve your custom CSS and code so it isn't wiped out when the parent theme receives an update
To create a second, backup copy of the whole website
To let two developers log in with the same account

questions.q: What is the main risk of installing too many WordPress plugins, known as 'Plugin Bloat'?
options: The dashboard changes color
It can slow down the site, cause conflicts between plugins, and create security vulnerabilities
WordPress automatically deletes old posts
It has no real downside, more plugins is always better

questions.q: Before updating the WordPress core or installing a major plugin, what is the single most important action a professional developer must take first?
options: Change the site's color scheme
Perform a complete database and file backup
Delete all existing plugins
Log out of the dashboard
